problem_text:
A logistics company needs to distribute its total shipping volume across 20 different transportation routes to maximize total expected delivery efficiency.  
The characteristics of each route are as follows:  
* Route A: expected efficiency is 0.104, operational complexity is 0.099, allocation bounds [0.032, 0.575]  
* Route B: expected efficiency is 0.026, operational complexity is 0.145, allocation bounds [0.060, 0.399]  
* Route C: expected efficiency is 0.041, operational complexity is 0.064, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.301]  
* Route D: expected efficiency is 0.138, operational complexity is 0.016, allocation bounds [0.031, 0.388]  
* Route E: expected efficiency is 0.054, operational complexity is 0.245, allocation bounds [0.002, 0.830]  
* Route F: expected efficiency is 0.045, operational complexity is 0.142, allocation bounds [0.039, 0.481]  
* Route G: expected efficiency is 0.126, operational complexity is 0.177, allocation bounds [0.071, 0.348]  
* Route H: expected efficiency is 0.087, operational complexity is 0.136, allocation bounds [0.068, 0.442]  
* Route I: expected efficiency is 0.088, operational complexity is 0.126, allocation bounds [0.074, 0.422]  
* Route J: expected efficiency is 0.126, operational complexity is 0.252, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.354]  
* Route K: expected efficiency is 0.026, operational complexity is 0.083, allocation bounds [0.015, 0.447]  
* Route L: expected efficiency is 0.146, operational complexity is 0.118, allocation bounds [0.075, 0.711]  
* Route M: expected efficiency is 0.133, operational complexity is 0.108, allocation bounds [0.058, 0.807]  
* Route N: expected efficiency is 0.176, operational complexity is 0.207, allocation bounds [0.010, 0.525]  
* Route O: expected efficiency is 0.021, operational complexity is 0.097, allocation bounds [0.026, 0.586]  
* Route P: expected efficiency is 0.096, operational complexity is 0.292, allocation bounds [0.074, 0.507]  
* Route Q: expected efficiency is 0.080, operational complexity is 0.264, allocation bounds [0.075, 0.582]  
* Route R: expected efficiency is 0.137, operational complexity is 0.231, allocation bounds [0.024, 0.712]  
* Route S: expected efficiency is 0.038, operational complexity is 0.271, allocation bounds [0.059, 0.719]  
* Route T: expected efficiency is 0.184, operational complexity is 0.157, allocation bounds [0.062, 0.848]  

Each route must receive a proportion of the total shipping volume that stays within its individual lower and upper bounds, and the sum of all allocation proportions must equal one.  
To ensure sufficient coverage of high-priority routes, the company requires that the group of key routes, represented by the subset K = {C, D, E, F, G, H, I, L, M, O, P, Q, T}, collectively receive at least 0.728 of the total shipping volume.  
At the same time, the overall operational complexity of the distribution plan, measured by a composite complexity index, must not exceed 0.222, and the total expected delivery efficiency must be no less than 0.069.  
Determine the optimal shipping volume allocation across routes that maximizes total expected efficiency while satisfying all constraints.
